name: SurrealDB
license: Business Source License 1.1 (becomes Apache 2.0 on 1 January 2030 for 3.0)
summary: A multi-model database in Rust that stores documents, graph edges, vectors and time series in one engine, queried with an SQL-like language, SurrealQL, and able to run embedded, as a server or as a cluster.
intro: SurrealDB keeps records in tables, each with an ID like `person:aristotle`, and lets a table be schemaless JSON or fully typed. Records can link to each other directly, and `RELATE` creates graph edges stored as records in an edge table, with `in` and `out` fields and data of their own, so `SELECT ->wrote->article FROM person:aristotle` walks the graph. The same engine does full-text and vector search, geospatial and time-series queries. SurrealQL keeps the shape of SQL and adds graph traversals, nested field access and similarity functions, and transactions can span many rows and tables.

Access control is part of the database: `DEFINE TABLE ... PERMISSIONS` rules decide per table and field what each signed-in user may read and write, using `$auth`, so a front end can query the database directly. `LIVE SELECT` subscribes a client to changes on a table or a filtered set of records, delivered as full records or JSON Patch diffs.

The query layer is separate from storage. One binary runs in memory (SurrealMX), on disk with RocksDB or the in-house SurrealKV (still beta), in the browser on IndexedDB, embedded in Rust, Go, JavaScript, Python or .NET programs, or as a multi-node cluster on shared distributed storage in SurrealDB Cloud and the self-hosted Enterprise edition. Every engine gives snapshot isolation with write conflicts detected at commit. Version 3.0 came out in February 2026; the 3.x source is under the Business Source License, which allows production use but not offering SurrealDB as a database service to others, and turns into Apache 2.0 on 1 January 2030.
strengths: Documents, graph edges, vectors and full-text search in one engine and one query language, in one transaction
Row- and field-level permissions and live queries, so client apps can talk to it without an API layer in between
Runs anywhere from a browser tab or an embedded library to a managed cluster
SQL-like syntax that is quick to pick up for anyone who knows SQL
limits: Business Source License, not open source: you may not run it as a database service for others until the change date
Young compared with PostgreSQL or MongoDB, with a smaller ecosystem of tools, drivers and operators
Multi-node clusters on distributed storage are a Cloud and Enterprise feature; the open RocksDB and SurrealKV engines are single-node
SurrealQL is its own dialect, so SQL tools, ORMs and BI connectors don’t work with it as they are

goodFor.why: A table can be schemaless JSON or fully typed, and SurrealQL reaches into nested fields and links records directly.
The same engine embeds in Rust, Go, JavaScript, Python or .NET programs, or runs in a browser on IndexedDB.

specs.data-model: Multi-model: documents, graph edges, vectors and time series in tables
specs.query-language: SurrealQL, an SQL-like language with graph traversals
specs.secondary-indexes: Includes full-text and vector search indexes
specs.isolation: Snapshot isolation; write conflicts detected at commit
specs.scaling: Single node on RocksDB or SurrealKV; clusters on distributed storage in Cloud and Enterprise
specs.storage-engine: Pluggable: in memory (SurrealMX), RocksDB, SurrealKV (beta), IndexedDB, distributed storage
specs.deployment: Embedded, single server, self-hosted Enterprise cluster, or SurrealDB Cloud

snippet.title: SurrealQL: records, a graph edge, a permission rule and a live query
source: CREATE article:sleep SET title = 'On Sleep and Sleeplessness', published = true;
RELATE person:aristotle->wrote->article:sleep SET year = -350;   -- an edge record
SELECT name, ->wrote->article.title AS titles FROM person:aristotle;
FOR select WHERE published = true OR user = $auth.id
FOR create, update, delete WHERE user = $auth.id;
LIVE SELECT * FROM post WHERE published = true;   -- push changes to this client

story: Tobie and Jaime Morgan Hitchcock founded SurrealDB in London as one database for document and graph data, with access rules and real-time queries built in so that web apps could query it directly. The engine, written in Rust, was released publicly on GitHub in 2022.

A $6 million seed round followed in January 2023, and 1.0, the first stable release, came out in September 2023. In November 2025 the company raised a $38 million Series A, bringing its total to $44 million, and in February 2026 it released SurrealDB 3.0, the third major version of the engine, under a Business Source License that turns into Apache 2.0 in 2030.

choices.why: Apps that need documents, relationships, search and vectors usually stitch several databases together. Putting them in one engine lets one query and one transaction span all of them.

choices.choice: Permissions and live queries in the database
choices.why: If the database itself enforces who may read what and pushes changes, a front end can connect to it directly without a hand-written API server.
Any key-value engine that offers transactional reads and writes of keys and ranges can sit underneath, so the same query layer runs in a browser, on one disk or on distributed storage.
It lets anyone use SurrealDB in production while stopping other companies from selling it as a hosted service, and the 3.0 code becomes Apache 2.0 on 1 January 2030.
